item.title: I would've mixed it better on analog
item.description: The rapid evolution of technology allowed personal computers to gradually replace numerous task-specific machines, including those used in music production. As soon as it became possible, the concept of a recording studio got reimagined as a DAW (Digital Audio Workstation), packing almost all your fancy studio gear into a single shortcut on your computer screen. The ever-growing market of VST plugins saturated the picture even more, offering more virtual instruments and effects you knew existed. More often than not, musicians and producers began using state-of-the-art mixing consoles and gear racks as laptop stands.
